# Plans

Design documents and implementation plans: `design-<topic>.md`, `plan-<topic>.md`.

## Every document declares its status

```
**Status:** proposed (2026-09-09)
```

`proposed` means thinking aloud. **It is never authorization to build.** A document becomes
`ruled` when a person says so, and only then does implementation start. This is the convention
most often skipped under time pressure, and skipping it is how a proposal becomes a decision
nobody made.

## These documents are temporary

**After about eight days a working document is either implemented or obsolete, and either way it
goes.** If it was implemented, its rulings are already in `CHANGELOG.md`, because writing that
entry is part of landing the work. If it was obsolete, there was nothing to carry.

Do not sift. Where a document still holds something valuable, neither a person nor a model can
reliably tell it from the rest — so the attempt costs the effort and returns an answer you then
trust. Git keeps every deleted file.

**Deleting is not automatic.** List what is past eight days and ask; never delete unasked.

## Where the durable version lives

`CHANGELOG.md`. It is the only document whose update is a side effect of the very work that would
otherwise invalidate it — which is why a ruling recorded there stays true, and a ruling recorded
only in a plan rots with the plan.

## Accumulating and rolling

This directory **accumulates**: one more file per piece of work, and a growing set is one nobody
re-reads. That is why the eight-day rule applies here.

A document that is overwritten in place — a task list, a handoff, a generated index — **rolls**,
and is current by construction. Its age is a reason to update it, not to delete it. Prune its
stale entries instead.

## What does not belong here

- Audit findings → `project/audits/`
- Audit procedures → `docs/audits/`
- Active tasks → `project/TODO.md`
- Decisions that must outlive the work → `CHANGELOG.md`
